thread:
maya_support: Hi @acme_ops — we're starting an investigation into the recent p95 latency spikes. Can you provide a short set of request ids (5-10) that hit during the window and a representative prompt sample?

acme_ops: thanks, will gather. quick Q — should we include auth headers or scrub them?

maya_support: please redact secrets but keep the X-Request-ID and X-Account-ID headers intact. those are critical.

alex_perf: to triage we also need: model name + revision, region, whether the client used streaming, input tokens vs generated tokens, and approximate concurrency at the time. a tiny csv is fine.

julia_support: to capture local traces, run this debug helper and upload the zip: 
```bash
# on customer host
rwi-cli collect-debug --request-ids req_XXXXX,req_YYYYY --include-har --concurrency-sample 64 --out acme-debug.zip
```

sam_eng_infra: and please collect a short concurrency profile using our wrapper (3 minutes at target concurrency):
```bash
./stress-client --url https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat --concurrency 120 --duration 180 --save profile-120.json
```
this helps us reproduce batching behavior.

acme_ops: sharing 5 ids now: req_202403_1, req_202403_2, req_202403_3, req_202403_4, req_202403_5. attaching a sample prompt (3 variations) and a small token histogram from our side. also here's a curl we used: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Request-ID: req_202403_1" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"Summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

maya_support: got it, thanks. starting artifact assembly. we'll fetch service-side logs for those ids and correlate with your HAR. expect initial findings in ~4 hours.

alex_perf: quick pointer — we often see p95 regressions when small batches interleave with long-running KV cache misses. can you also confirm whether prefix caching and batching were enabled client-side?

acme_ops: confirmed: client-side batching=on, caching=off. some requests had long generation ( >600 tokens ).

julia_support: if possible, run a short controlled replay: 10 minutes at 70% peak RPS and one at 130% peak to show graceful degradation. use this wrk command (streaming-aware):
```bash
w rk -t8 -c200 -d600 -s tools/stream.lua --latency https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat
```
(we can provide the script if you don't have it)

sam_eng_infra: also include a memory/cpu scrape (Prometheus or top output) during the replay. fields we need: GPU util, host CPU, network bytes, swap.

acme_ops: uploading debug bundle and profile-120.json to the S3 link you provided. available for a live session 17:00 PST.

repro-bot: automated: debug bundles for req_202403_1..5 uploaded (s3://redwood-debug/acme/191234/debug-acme-1912340000.zip). logs indexed under trace IDs trace-ACME-191234.

maya_support: thanks @repro-bot and @acme_ops — assigning this to eng-perf for deeper analysis. tagging @alex_perf @sam_eng_infra. we'll follow up after correlating traces.

alex_perf: thanks all. immediate next steps from perf: (1) validate token histogram against server-side batching bins, (2) replay at similar concurrency in our QA cluster, (3) check kernel selection logs for the model revision. I'll post findings here once the replay completes.

acme_ops: appreciate it — will stand by for results. if you want more request ids from a different day I can grab them.

maya_support: perfect. if we need a calendar slot we'll request one for the 17:00 PST window you offered. otherwise we'll share a repro bundle and recommended mitigation (likely batching tweak or short-term capacity bump). :thumbsup:

julia_support: closing loop for now — please let us know if latency shows up again after the next config change.

acme_ops: will do, thanks team!"
